constraints.prompt: Diverse 14-day vegetarian week — keep formats varied (don't stack 3 bowls in a row), pull cuisine fusions when they fit, and lean on the household's signature flavor vibes (gochujang aioli is elite, miso butter, preserved lemon everywhere).
constraints.menu_rationale: This 14-day plan addresses urgent pantry pressure (shiitake and swiss chard expiring days 2–3) and restrained anchor use. The household recently saturated on chickpea, tahini, and asparagus (all at 1.00 pressure), so this week deploys them sparingly—chickpea in only 2 dinners (curry, wrap), tahini in 2 (sauce applications), asparagus in 2 (risotto, omelette)—ensuring freshness rather than fatigue. Format variety is paramount: flatbread, risotto, grain bowl, burger, taco, pizza, omelette, and stir-fry replace the recently heavy rotations (pasta, skillet, soup appear sparingly). Cuisine spreads across Italian (risotto, omelette, pizza), Mediterranean (flatbreads, salads, grain bowl), Levantine (wrap, final flatbread), Japanese (stir-fry), Indian (curry), Thai (curry), and Mexican (tacos), balanced with the cuisine-direction hints but never dominated by them. Signature flavor vibes anchor every third dinner: gochujang-aioli smashburger (Korean fusion), miso-butter risotto (Japanese-Italian), harissa-honey flatbread (North African), preserved-lemon omelette (Mediterranean), and tahini-lemon grain bowl all deliver the household's proven elevations. Leftovers drive 8 of 14 lunches (curry, risotto, flatbreads, stir-fry, pizza), keeping prep lean and sustainable. Breakfasts balance quick jars (chia, overnight oats) with 3 cooked options (scramble, shakshuka, avocado toast with egg), and snack boxes follow a mezze structure with dip + crunch + fruit + savory across 7 offerings.

prep_tasks.title: Make Lemon Tahini Sauce
instructions: Whisk 6 tbsp tahini with 4 tbsp lemon juice — it will seize and look broken.
Add ice water 1 tbsp at a time, whisking constantly, until silky and pourable (typically 4-6 tbsp total).
Stir in 1 clove garlic and 0.5 tsp salt. Taste and balance.
Transfer to a jar; pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator. Loosens with cold storage — re-whisk with a splash of water before serving.

prep_tasks.title: Make Herb Yogurt Sauce
instructions: In food processor, blitz 1 cup parsley + 1/2 cup dill + 1/4 cup mint with 1 clove garlic and 0.5 tsp salt until finely chopped.
Fold into 1 cup yogurt with 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil.
Taste; adjust salt and lemon. Mixture should be brightly green and tangy.
Transfer to a jar; pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator. Flavor improves after 30 min rest.

prep_tasks.title: Make Cooked Whole Chickpeas
instructions: Soak the dried chickpeas overnight in cold water with a pinch of baking soda; drain and rinse.
Combine soaked chickpeas with 4 cup water and 1 tsp salt in the instant pot.
Cook on bean/chili setting for 35 min, then natural release for 15 min.
Skim any foam; reserve 1 cup of the cooking liquid (aquafaba) — useful for hummus.
Cool to room temperature, then pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator.

prep_tasks.title: Make Quick Pickled Radishes
instructions: Slice radishes paper-thin on a mandoline (1-2 mm).
In a small saucepan, warm 1 cup rice vinegar with 2 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt just until dissolved.
Pack the sliced radishes into a clean jar; pour the warm brine over to cover.
Cool on the counter for 30 min, then refrigerate. Ready to eat after 1 hour; best after 24h.
pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator — keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

prep_tasks.title: Make Hummus
instructions: In food processor, combine 4 tbsp tahini and 2 tbsp lemon juice; whip 90 seconds until light and creamy.
Add 2 clove garlic, 1 tsp salt, and 2 tbsp ice water; pulse to combine.
Add the cooked chickpeas in two batches, processing 2-3 minutes between each, until ultra smooth.
Drizzle in olive oil while running until silky. Taste and adjust salt + lemon.
Transfer to a wide, shallow container; smooth top, drizzle with olive oil; store in refrigerator.

prep_tasks.title: Make Crispy Chickpeas
instructions: Drain cooked chickpeas thoroughly and pat completely dry with a kitchen towel — moisture is the enemy of crisp.
Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, 0.5 tsp salt, and any spices (cumin, smoked paprika, sumac).
Spread on a sheet pan in single layer. Roast at 425°F for 25-30 min, shaking the pan every 10 min, until deeply golden and crisp.
Cool fully on the sheet pan (chickpeas crisp further as they cool).
pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator but DO NOT seal until cold — trapped steam ruins the crunch. Best eaten within 72h.

prep_tasks.title: Check active technique branches
instructions: Confirm the week is using: bake, drain, slice, roast.

prep_tasks.title: Make Chia Pudding
instructions: In a jar, whisk 5 tbsp chia seed with 1.5 cup milk, 1 tbsp maple syrup, and 1 tsp vanilla.
Whisk hard for 30 seconds; rest 5 min; whisk again to break up clumps.
Seal and pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator for at least 4h or overnight. Stir before serving.
Top with fresh fruit, granola, or nut butter when serving.

prep_tasks.title: Make Overnight Oats
instructions: In a jar, combine 1 cup rolled oats with 1 cup milk and 0.5 cup yogurt.
Sweeten with 1 tbsp maple syrup; add 1.5 tbsp chia seed for body and a splash of vanilla.
Stir well, seal, and refrigerate at least 8h or overnight.
pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator. Top with fresh fruit + nut butter when serving.

prep_tasks.title: Make Cold-Fermented Dough
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk 3.2 cup all-purpose flour with 1.5 tsp salt and 2 tsp yeast.
Add 1.1 cup water (65% hydration) and 1 tbsp olive oil; mix until shaggy. Cover; rest 20 min.
Stretch-and-fold the dough in the bowl 4 times, every 15 min, over the next hour.
Divide into desired portions (4 pita-size or 2 pizza-size); shape into tight balls.
Place balls in oiled containers, spaced apart; pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator. Cold ferment 48-72h for best flavor — pull from fridge 1-2h before shaping/baking.

prep_tasks.title: Make Herb Yogurt Sauce
instructions: In food processor, blitz 1 cup parsley + 1/2 cup dill + 1/4 cup mint with 1 clove garlic and 0.5 tsp salt until finely chopped.
Fold into 1 cup yogurt with 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil.
Taste; adjust salt and lemon. Mixture should be brightly green and tangy.
Transfer to a jar; pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator. Flavor improves after 30 min rest.

prep_tasks.title: Make Hummus
instructions: In food processor, combine 4 tbsp tahini and 2 tbsp lemon juice; whip 90 seconds until light and creamy.
Add 2 clove garlic, 1 tsp salt, and 2 tbsp ice water; pulse to combine.
Add the cooked chickpeas in two batches, processing 2-3 minutes between each, until ultra smooth.
Drizzle in olive oil while running until silky. Taste and adjust salt + lemon.
Transfer to a wide, shallow container; smooth top, drizzle with olive oil; store in refrigerator.

instructions: Whisk 6 tbsp tahini with 4 tbsp lemon juice — it will seize and look broken.
Add ice water 1 tbsp at a time, whisking constantly, until silky and pourable (typically 4-6 tbsp total).
Stir in 1 clove garlic and 0.5 tsp salt. Taste and balance.
Transfer to a jar; pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator. Loosens with cold storage — re-whisk with a splash of water before serving.

prep_tasks.title: Make Chia Pudding
instructions: In a jar, whisk 5 tbsp chia seed with 1.5 cup milk, 1 tbsp maple syrup, and 1 tsp vanilla.
Whisk hard for 30 seconds; rest 5 min; whisk again to break up clumps.
Seal and pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator for at least 4h or overnight. Stir before serving.
Top with fresh fruit, granola, or nut butter when serving.

prep_tasks.title: Remake Cooked Whole Chickpeas (batch 2026-05-17)
instructions: Soak the dried chickpeas overnight in cold water with a pinch of baking soda; drain and rinse.
Combine soaked chickpeas with 4 cup water and 1 tsp salt in the instant pot.
Cook on bean/chili setting for 35 min, then natural release for 15 min.
Skim any foam; reserve 1 cup of the cooking liquid (aquafaba) — useful for hummus.
Cool to room temperature, then pack in a labeled airtight container; store in refrigerator.

meta.prompt: Diverse 14-day vegetarian week — keep formats varied (don't stack 3 bowls in a row), pull cuisine fusions when they fit, and lean on the household's signature flavor vibes (gochujang aioli is elite, miso butter, preserved lemon everywhere).

notes: Chia Pudding: 3 uses across 12 days exceeds 96h fridge — split into 3 batches
Herb Yogurt Sauce: 8 uses across 13 days exceeds 96h fridge — split into 3 batches
Cold-Fermented Dough: 4 uses across 13 days exceeds 96h fridge — split into 3 batches
Hummus: 2 uses across 6 days exceeds 96h fridge — split into 2 batches
Lemon Tahini Sauce: 4 uses across 10 days exceeds 120h fridge — split into 2 batches
Overnight Oats: 3 uses across 7 days exceeds 72h fridge — split into 2 batches
Quick Pickled Radishes: 4 uses across 9 days exceeds 168h fridge — split into 2 batches
Falafel Mix: 2 uses across 2 days exceeds 24h fridge — split into 2 batches

top_edges.rationale: A small cooked-bean split creates crunch for bowls and salads.
A loose tahini sauce bridges chickpeas, roasted vegetables, bowls, and flatbreads.
Cooked chickpeas plus tahini produce a durable snack-box dip.
A soaked split supports a project branch without committing the whole batch.
Soaking opens falafel and shorter cook-time branches.
Soaked chickpeas can still become a neutral cooked batch.
Dry chickpeas can become neutral cooked beans for several weekly components.
